threads.thread_goal: Align on target account list and pilot scope for the new device program.

messages.text: Team, kicking off the 'Launch of New Medical Device Education & Sales Program'. The first step is to define our pilot accounts. I've started the 'Target Account Segmentation Sheet' (A1) to track T1. Please add your top 5-7 accounts for the initial wave by EOD tomorrow.

Great start, @36427. I'm in A1 now. To ensure the educational content is tailored correctly, should we prioritize teaching hospitals or large private clinics? Having a clear focus will help me shape the materials.

Good question. My view is that teaching hospitals are key for driving adoption and creating advocates early on. They are often more receptive to new clinical data. I've added my list to A1 with a focus on those.
My accounts are in A1 now. What's the criteria for Tier 1 vs Tier 2? Is it based on bed count, specialty, or existing relationships?

@96324 Let's define Tier 1 as major teaching hospitals with strong research departments and an existing relationship. Tier 2 can be other large hospitals or clinics known for early adoption. I've added this to the sheet's header.
Sorry for the delay. I will add my accounts to A1 soon.
Thanks, @63661. Please try to get them in by noon so we can finalize the list.
That tiering logic works for me. It gives me a clear audience for the initial educational push.
Ok, I've added them to the sheet. Are we supposed to add private clinics too?

@63661 Thanks. For the pilot, let's stick to the hospital focus we just discussed to keep the scope tight. We can expand to private clinics in the next phase. I've filtered the list to just hospitals for now.
Looking at the combined list in A1, we have about 25 accounts. Is that too many for a 21-day pilot? Maybe we should cap it at 15-20 to ensure we can provide high-touch support.
I agree, 20 sounds more manageable.
Excellent point, @438092. Let's be realistic. How does everyone feel about a cap of 20 accounts for the first wave? We can select the top 5 from each of our lists.
20 is a solid number. That allows for meaningful data collection without spreading us too thin.
ok with me
Works for me. I'll highlight my top 5 in A1.
Sounds good. I've marked mine.

Perfect. It's settled then. Decision: We will include 20 accounts in the first pilot wave. (D2). I've updated A1 to reflect the final, prioritized list. Decision: The initial list of pilot accounts and priority tiers in A1 is approved. (D1). This completes T1.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise educational slide deck and sales script.

messages.text: Hi team, I've uploaded the first draft of the 'Clinician Educational Slide Deck v1' (A2) for T2. It covers the device's mechanism, clinical benefits, and safety profile. I'd appreciate your feedback on the flow and messaging before it goes for regulatory review. I've also started a skeleton for the 'Standard Sales Script and Objection Guide' (A3).

This is a fantastic start, @70832. The structure is very clear. My main feedback on A2: on slide 8, can we add a direct comparison table against the current standard of care? It would make the value prop more immediate. For A3, I'll add a section for handling the most common objections we anticipate.

I agree, A2 is very well-organized. The clinical data on slide 12 is compelling, but we should add a footnote clarifying the patient population of that study to preempt questions from specialists. It's a detail that will build credibility.
Looks good. For the objection guide A3, can we make sure to include a response for 'I'm happy with my current device'?
Excellent suggestions. @36427, a comparison table is a great idea, I'll build that in. @438092, good catch on the footnote, I'll add that detail. @96324, yes, that's a critical one for A3.
Where can I find the deck?
@63661 I linked it in my first message, it's document A2. Let me know if you have trouble accessing it.
Absolutely, @96324. I've added that and a few others to A3. It's ready for the team to review now.
found it. looks ok to me.
I've incorporated all the feedback into a v1.1 of the deck A2. Unless there are any other major comments, I think we can agree on the final structure and key messages.
The new version of A2 looks solid. The comparison table and footnote add a lot of clarity.

Looks great, @70832. Let's lock it in. Decision: We agree on the final structure and key messages of the educational slide deck (A2) (D3). The sales script and objection guide (A3) also looks ready for the pilot. Decision: We approve the standard sales script and objection-handling guide for use in the pilot (D4). I'll flag these for the regulatory team.
Perfect. This completes T2 and T3 for now. I'll await feedback from regulatory and be ready for any refinements needed for T12.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the digital outreach plan and webinar schedule.

messages.text: Team, please find the draft 'Digital Outreach Plan for New Device' (A4). For the pilot, I'm proposing we focus on two channels: targeted email campaigns to our list in A1, and regular posts on LinkedIn to build awareness. I've also outlined three potential webinar topics as part of T4 and T7. What are your thoughts?

This is great, @70832. Focusing on LinkedIn and email makes sense for a targeted HCP audience. The webinar topics are spot on. I can map the target accounts from A1 to each topic to maximize relevance.

I like the plan. For the LinkedIn content, we could create short video clips from the educational deck (A2) to make the posts more engaging. Highlighting the key data points visually could be very effective.
The plan looks good. When are you thinking of holding the webinars? We should avoid Mondays and Fridays if possible.
Love the video clip idea, @438092. I can definitely create those. @96324, I was thinking mid-week, either Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon. I'll propose some specific dates for the first one next week.
what about twitter?

@63661 Good question. While some clinicians are on Twitter, LinkedIn is generally where we see more professional engagement with medical device content. To keep our efforts focused during the pilot, let's stick to LinkedIn and email for now.
Agreed. Let's master two channels before expanding. So, are we aligned on the approach?
Yes, aligned.
Yes, sounds like a solid plan.

Great. Decision: We will use LinkedIn and targeted email as the primary digital channels for the pilot, with video clips as a key content type (D5). I will now schedule the first webinar for next Wednesday, targeting the Tier 1 accounts from A1. Decision: The date is confirmed for the first webinar, with the target list defined (D6). This moves T7 forward.
Excellent. The sales team will start sending out personal invitations tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Align on CRM logging, KPIs and reporting expectations.

messages.text: Hi all, as we get closer to the pilot launch, we need to lock down our tracking process. @70832 has prepared the 'KPI Tracking Dashboard Template' (A6) for T6, and I've drafted the 'CRM Logging Process' (A8) for T10. Please review both and share any questions.
Thanks @36427. The first tab in A6 has definitions for each KPI, like 'lead', 'demo scheduled', and 'order'. The goal is to have a single source of truth for pilot performance.

Thanks for putting these together. The KPI definitions in A6 are helpful. For the CRM process A8, can we clarify if a 'follow-up email' counts as a logged interaction? Or is it only calls and meetings?
Good question, @96324. Let's log all substantive interactions, including emails where new information is shared or questions are answered. I'll add that clarification to A8.

The KPI set looks good. I'd suggest adding one qualitative field to the CRM logging process in A8: 'Key Clinical Question'. This would help us track recurring themes in the questions we get, which is valuable feedback for marketing and medical affairs.
That's a brilliant idea, @438092. It's much more specific than a generic 'notes' field. I've added it to A8.
Do we have to use the 'Pre-Call Compliance and Materials Checklist' A5 for every call?

Yes, @63661. Using A5 is mandatory. It's a critical step to ensure we are all using the correct, approved materials and staying compliant. It also serves as a reminder to log the interaction in the CRM afterward.
I really like that suggestion @438092. That data will be invaluable for the post-pilot report.
Ok, that's clear now. The process looks good to me.

Okay team, it sounds like we have consensus. Decision: The KPI set and definitions in A6 are final for the pilot (D7). Decision: The CRM logging process in A8, including the new 'Key Clinical Question' field, is confirmed (D8). Let's make sure we all start using this from day one of the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Share pilot results, feedback and decide on broader rollout.

messages.text: Team, the initial pilot period has concluded. The full data is updated in the 'KPI Tracking Dashboard' (A6), and I've shared a draft of the 'Post-Pilot Performance and Lessons Report' (A7) which summarizes T11. A key finding from the call feedback (T8) is that while clinical interest is high, we're consistently facing questions about cost-effectiveness that we need to address better.

Thanks for compiling this, @70832. The report reflects what I've been hearing on my calls. The cost question is definitely the biggest hurdle. We need to update our sales script (A3) to proactively frame the value conversation around long-term savings and improved outcomes, not just upfront cost.

I was just looking at the data in A6. It's interesting that our conversion rate from demo to order was highest with the Tier 2 accounts, not Tier 1. My hypothesis is that the larger teaching hospitals have more complex purchasing committees and budget cycles. This might mean we need to rethink our targeting strategy for a full rollout.
I agree on the cost issue. I had two promising conversations stall completely when procurement got involved. Having some pre-approved language for that in the script would be a huge help.
That's a fantastic insight, @438092. I've added a note about that in the report A7. It's a crucial learning from the pilot.
yes the calls were hard when they asked about money.

You're right, @438092. The data in A6 is clear. We shouldn't abandon Tier 1, but we need a different approach for them, perhaps a longer sales cycle. For the immediate broader rollout, we should probably focus on the Tier 2 profile. This means we need to adjust our target account strategy.
That makes sense. Focus on the accounts that can move faster to build momentum.

Okay, let's make two key decisions based on these excellent pilot learnings. First, Decision: We will adjust the target account strategy to prioritize 'Tier 2' profile accounts for the initial phase of the full rollout, based on pilot conversion data (D1). Second, Decision: We will update the sales script (A3) to include stronger value-based arguments to address cost objections before the full rollout (D4).
I'll finalize the report A7 with these decisions as the main recommendations. Great work everyone, this is exactly what a pilot is for.
